title: fix: Claude CLI forgets announced sub-agent results on the next turn
body:
Fixes #171195

Related: #159512 (completion-session isolation), #154716 (native-login history ownership).

## What Problem This Solves

A Claude CLI requester can announce a completed sub-agent's result, then resume an older native session on the next user turn and claim that the child has not reported back.

## User Impact

The next resumed turn receives recorded completion exchanges when its existing history account boundary permits replay. When content is withheld, the turn receives a metadata-only gap notice that includes those completions. Tool restrictions and account boundaries stay in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI history owner reads pending completion exchanges from the canonical transcript, distinguishing ordinary replies, state-preserving handoffs, and background refreshes. An ordinary reply consumes the carry. The newest eight exchanges use the existing context JSON sanitizer and its 2,000-character string limit. The renderer requires the existing history writer; the existing transport revalidates that authority immediately before disclosure. No parallel store, schema change, or new configuration is introduced.

The wording covers both isolated and already-resumed completion turns, and tells the model to verify current facts before acting on historical records. The original user prompt remains the stored transcript input, and native-history import strips the marked context.

Original fix by @etzelm; maintainer cleanup consolidates rendering in the transcript owner, removes duplicate sanitization and exports, and replaces the large subprocess/live-probe additions with focused owner regressions.

## Evidence

PR CI is the test gate under the maintainer's October 13, 2026 proof policy. Local tests, typechecks, negative controls, live Gateway proofs, Crabbox, and Testbox were intentionally skipped. No contributor runtime code executed on the host.

Regression coverage for CI:

- `preserved Claude turns > carries completion exchanges since the last ordinary reply, or counts them when content is withheld`: real transcript writes/readback, reply-only announcements, queued provenance, background refreshes, fresh-session exclusion, one-turn consumption, bounded carry and sanitization.
- `CLI resume user context`: drift ordering, fresh-session exclusion, and withholding without the history writer.
- `imported Claude history merge > shows a resumed turn carrying unseen exchanges once`: marked completion context imports without a duplicate user turn, with and without drift.
- Existing session-history and routed-prompt tests cover stripping the metadata-only note.

Changed-file oxlint and oxfmt pass. The parent install lacks the unrelated Solid lint plugin, so local lint used the repository's core rules with only the `ui/**/*.tsx` override omitted; no changed file matches that override. Deslop removed redundant production helpers and duplicate proof scaffolding. Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2; no actionable findings. The reviewed production patch is unchanged by the main merge; its only conflict retained main's reduced routed-prompt test matrix and added the new completion-gap case. **Exact-head [CI run 38468757728](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38468757728) passed** on `70b6de0a26bd9ff568cd7700e42748a98bcc3358`: changed Node/Bun test lanes, production types, all core test-type shards, lint, docs, source/architecture guards, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. No failed checks or inherited-failure exceptions. The only merge conflict was the routed-prompt test matrix; main's reduction was retained with one new completion-gap case.

Source/history confirmation: main's `renderClaudeSessionGap` chooses the latest `claude-cli` assistant row without distinguishing `announce:` replies; `subagent_announce` preserves the requester binding. That combination both loses the carried result and hides the metadata gap. The original gap change is #168726. Collision checks found only this PR for #171195.

ClawSweeper's exact-head review (October 13, 21:21 UTC) reports **no code findings** and explicitly identifies no concrete account-boundary bypass. The topology-wording finding is resolved; the older live-probe matcher finding is superseded by removal of that optional probe. Its remaining security/merge-risk attention is an evidence request for live completion/resume and final-input authority-denial traces. Per the maintainer's explicit proof policy for this task, PR CI is the proof; those proof-only requests do not add live, negative-control, or local test requirements. Existing writer/account assertions remain intact. Earlier persisted-binding concerns are superseded by the transcript-only design. There were no human review comments.

Diff against merged main: production +136/-19 (net +117), tests +253/-6 (net +247), docs +18/-1 (net +17); 11 files, +407/-26 overall. No new timers, sleeps, subprocesses, or Gateway boots; local test wall time is intentionally unmeasured. CI recorded the transcript regression at 1,297 ms (one test; 14.32 s Vitest / 16.49 s shard wall including imports), the three new renderer cases at 2 ms each (the existing file's full run: eight tests, 43.38 s Vitest / 45.27 s shard wall, dominated by pre-existing runtime imports), and the two import cases at 32 ms and 10 ms. No additional subprocess harness is needed for these owner contracts. Production growth is necessary to classify the previously unrepresented completion boundary and render its bounded context; unrelated deletions were not used to meet a negative-LOC target.
